title: Who went quiet?
prompt: On-call wants a freshness check over `application_logs`: for every service in `EXPECTED`, when it last logged before the check time, and whether that's recent enough. It must give the same answer when rerun later for the same check time. Complete `freshness`.
rules: Columns and types: `service STRING, last_log TIMESTAMP, quiet_s BIGINT, freshness STRING`, one row per service in `EXPECTED`. Other services are ignored.
Only logs at or before the check time count. `quiet_s` is the whole seconds from `last_log` to the check time, as `F.unix_timestamp` gives them.
`freshness` is `fresh` when `quiet_s` is at most `MAX_SILENCE_S`, `stale` when it's more, and `silent` when the service has no log at all by then (with NULL `last_log` and `quiet_s`).
hints: Run the starter on the sample. Which expected service has no row, and which row is about a log after the check time?
Grouping can't produce a row for a service with no logs. Stack a row per expected service with a NULL time onto the logs first, with `unionByName`; `F.max` ignores the NULLs.
Never use `F.current_timestamp()`: compare with the check time you were given, cast to a timestamp.
explanation: Filter the logs to the expected services and to times at or before the check time; a log stamped after it didn't exist yet when the check was due, and counting it would make a rerun disagree with the original run. A service that never logged has no rows to group, so it would vanish instead of raising the loudest alarm. Stacking one row per expected service with a NULL `logged_at` (`unionByName`) gives every service a group, and `F.max` skips the NULL, leaving `last_log` NULL only for the silent ones. `F.unix_timestamp` turns both times into whole seconds, so the difference is the silence, and exactly the limit is still fresh. Joining to a list of services would also work, but grouping and stacking is enough here.
